Automated Model Briefing

⚠ AI-generated text — may be wrong, incomplete, or overconfident. This is automated commentary on experimental model output, not flight advice and not a weather forecast. It has not been reviewed by a meteorologist.

Overall Assessment — Sunday is a poor flying day. Solid overcast, low and lowering cloud bases, and light snow showers spreading over several launches from about 1pm to 4pm. Southwest wind across the Sierra crest is moderate in the morning (22–25 knots) and eases to 10–16 knots in the afternoon. Daydreams is the only site with steady, well-aligned ridge lift, and even there the cloud base sits just above launch.

Site Breakdown

No site rated favorable today.

Not recommended today (9) — click a row for details

Hallelujah Marginal — Light, variable wind and weak thermals give only a short midday chance before cloud lowers and snow arrives around 2pm.
Window: 11am–1pm
Thermal strength peaks at 92–118 ft/min, below a paraglider's sink rate. The thermal top (PBLH) is about 1,250–1,500 ft above ground (AGL). Wind turns to a light 3–6 mph from 303–337° around 11am–1pm. Ridge lift of +68 to +145 ft/min is not enough to soar. Morning wind (8–10am) is from 144–190°, outside the launch direction. The lowest cloud drops from 1,600 ft above launch at 11am to 900 ft at 1pm and onto launch by 2pm. Light snow falls 2–4pm on a below-freezing launch (29–31 °F), so expect a wet or iced wing and lines then.
McClellan Marginal — Light wind on launch makes it sled-only, with no thermals and stronger wind aloft.
Window: 10am–1pm
Thermal strength is 0 ft/min all day, so expect sled rides only. Launch wind is a light 3–6 mph from 127–166° in the window, within the launch range. Ridge lift is +50 to +120 ft/min, and stable air partly flows around the lower slope. Wind 3,000 ft above ground is 20–25 mph from the southwest, with 23 mph of speed change between the surface and about 1,600 ft. Cloud base is 2,300–3,600 ft above launch. The launch is below freezing (25–31 °F).
Daydreams Marginal — Ridge lift is steady and strong, but the cloud base is barely above launch, the launch is below freezing, and wind sits on the west edge of the launch direction.
Window: 11am–1pm
Ridge lift is +280 to +336 ft/min in the window, with 14–18 mph lowest-layer wind from 247–251°. Launch wind is 12–16 mph from 251–263°. Thermal strength is 191–216 ft/min. The thermal top is about 1,600–1,750 ft above ground, but cloud base (the height a rising thermal forms cloud) is only 120–344 ft above launch, so climbs are capped very low. Morning cloud is a little higher (cloud base 484–710 ft above launch), but launch wind at 9–10am is 268–270°, west of the preferred 195–255°. Cloud base reaches launch level from 2pm to 3pm. The launch is 25–27 °F, so stay out of cloud to avoid icing.
Kingsbury grade Unfavorable — West wind all day blows over the back of this southeast-facing launch, and there are no thermals.
Thermal strength (w*) is 0 ft/min all day. Launch wind is 2–13 mph from 230–281°, well off the preferred 104°. Ridge lift is negative almost every hour (down to -95 ft/min), meaning sinking air on the launch face. The launch is below freezing (28–31 °F). How fast air cools with height (lapse rate) is 8.2 °C/km, which would normally mean sharp thermals for advanced pilots only, but the model shows no usable thermals here.
Slide Mountain Unfavorable — Strong southwest wind puts the launch on the downwind (sinking) side, and cloud sits on launch at midday with light snow.
Launch wind is 8–18 mph from 206–259°, outside the south-to-southeast launch direction. Ridge lift is strongly negative all day (-180 to -536 ft/min). Wind 1,000–3,000 ft above ground is 30–39 mph through midday. The lowest cloud is about 100 ft above launch from 12pm to 2pm, and light snow falls 1–2pm. Peak thermal strength is only 103 ft/min, and the launch is 20–23 °F.
West McClellan Unfavorable — Wind is mostly from the south, crossed to this west launch, and the only better-aligned hours bring lowering cloud and freezing rain.
Launch wind is 164–225° most of the day, outside the preferred 240–300°, and there are no thermals (0 ft/min after 10am). At 2–3pm the lowest wind turns to 238–239° and ridge lift reaches +144 to +215 ft/min. In those hours the cloud base is only 900–1,000 ft above launch, and light rain falls at 3pm with the launch below freezing (19–30 °F), which would ice the wing.
Peavine Mountain Unfavorable — Wind is too strong in the morning, and cloud sits at or on launch from midday.
Launch wind is 20–24 mph from 204–228° through 11am, then 14–19 mph from 229–240°. Ridge lift is negative all day (-62 to -129 ft/min). Thermal strength peaks at 152 ft/min, but the thermal top is only about 870 ft above ground. Cloud base is 100 ft or less above launch from 12pm to 4pm, so launch is likely in cloud. Wind 1,000 ft above ground is 30–32 mph in the morning. The launch is 21–22 °F.
Rainbow Ridge Unfavorable — Southwest-to-northwest wind blows over the back of this east-facing launch, and light snow follows.
Launch wind is 4–9 mph from 176–328° from 8am to 3pm, far from the preferred 67°. The 4pm wind is from 109° but only 1 mph. Thermal strength peaks at 120 ft/min at 1pm. Light snow falls 3–4pm, with the lowest cloud dropping to 100–500 ft above launch.
Duck Hill Unfavorable — Southeast wind is a tailwind for this west-to-north launch until it fades to calm late in the day.
Launch wind is 7–9 mph from 142–161° from 8am to 12pm, behind the launch. There are no thermals (0 ft/min). Wind only swings to 348–39° at 1–5 mph in the 3–4pm hours, with ridge lift of at most +37 ft/min, which is too weak for an evening soaring window before sunset.

Hazards

  • Morning mountain wave and wind shear: NWS Reno expects southwest winds near 10,000 ft of about 30 knots, bringing low-level wind shear (LLWS) and mountain wave turbulence through Sunday morning, and ridge gusts of 50–70 mph overnight into early Sunday. The model's crest-level wind is 25 knots from 225° at 8am, right at the threshold for rotor and downslope wind, then 22–23 knots from about 210° (slightly south of the most rotor-prone direction) and 10–16 knots after noon. The model does not clearly show the morning risk, so treat the lee of the Carson Range and Peavine as suspect in the morning.
  • Strong wind aloft at high launches: Wind 1,000–3,000 ft above ground is 30–39 mph at Slide Mountain and 30–35 mph at Peavine Mountain through late morning, much stronger than at launch.
  • Cloud on launch and low cloud base: Cloud base is at or within about 100 ft of launch at Peavine Mountain from 12pm to 4pm and at Slide Mountain from 12pm to 2pm. At Daydreams, cloud base falls to launch level from 2pm to 3pm. Visibility is not modeled, so check pilot reports and webcams.
  • Snow, freezing rain and wing icing: Light snow falls at Slide Mountain 1–2pm, Hallelujah 2–4pm and Rainbow Ridge 3–4pm, and light rain falls at West McClellan at 3pm on a launch below freezing. Most launches are at or below freezing all day, so any precipitation means a wet or iced wing and lines. NWS Reno gives a 20–40% chance of rain or a rain-snow mix in the Reno, Carson City and Minden areas starting late Sunday morning, a little earlier than the model shows.
